thread:
sam: Alert — multiple latency reports hitting today at ~22:10 UTC for /v1/chat/stream. p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~1.2s, p99 up to ~3.8s. Opening this thread for quick mitigations + repro. cc @rita @mike :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: INC-3454 created: latency spike detected on cluster us-west-2. p95=1.2s p99=3.8s error_rate=0.3% routes affected: /v1/chat/stream (gptx-4q variants). Link: https://observability.redwood/alerts/INC-3454
rita: Looking now. Any customer repros or payload examples? Which exact model variant and region?
sam: Customer A reported slow completions after the gptx-4q rollout last night. Route: POST /v1/chat/stream model=gptx-4q-0.9 region=us-west-2. Typical payload ~512 tokens, streaming enabled. Their support ticket includes this repro curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXX' \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-4q-0.9","input":"<~512 tokens>","stream":true}'
```
mike: I'm seeing queue depth rise on serving-pool nodes pool-51..54. CPU iowait and NVMe queueing spikes. Looks like batching backlog + disk pressure for swap/kv-cache. Might be an interaction with the new quantized kernel.
elaine: We should prepare a short customer note + fallback plan. If us-west2 still degraded, route paid customers to eu-central or enable the float (gptx-4f) fallback.
rita: Proposed mitigation ladder (doable in ~10-30m):
1) Apply per-route temporary rate limiting for free tiers and unverified clients (raise 429s for heavy clients).
2) Reduce BATCH_MAX from 32 -> 8 on affected pools to decrease tail latency.
3) Enable circuit breaker to short-circuit requests above concurrency threshold (return 429 fast).
4) Route critical customers to fallback model gptx-4f (float) in eu-central and mark requests with mitigation tag for billing trace.
Config snippets I'm pushing now:
```
# rate-limit rule
{"route":"/v1/chat/stream","condition":"client_tier==free","limit_per_min":200}

# circuit breaker env
{"CB_CONCURRENCY": 400, "CB_BACKOFF_MS": 150}
```
sam: Also enable prefix KV cache for warm chat sessions and prefer cold-start-safe models for very short requests (<=64 tokens). That should reduce token-level tail.
mike: Applying batch-size change now:
```
kubectl patch deploy serving-pool-51 -n infra --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/1/value","value":"8"}]'
```
I'll watch the autoscaler and node metrics.
rita: Patch applied to pool-51..54. Within ~6m p95 dropped to ~380ms, p99 at ~1.1s. Enabling regional fallback for critical customers next. Notifying support to inform Customer A. :thumbsup: 
elaine: Support updated customer A and published temporary status note. Please tag fallback requests with `mitigation=soft-fallback` so billing and cost reports attribute correctly.
sam: Post-incident follow-ups to create (INF-7890): capture repro steps, collect kernel logs from affected nodes, perf profile quantized kernels, and evaluate queue-based autoscale vs more aggressive circuit breakers. Also recommend exposing per-client rate-limit controls in Console. Filing ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7890
oncall-bot: INC-3454 resolved — metrics stable. final p95=220ms p99=480ms. Incident closed :white_check_mark:
